dimensions.name: Contract reverse-engineering & Excel-semantics grounding

evidence.note: Explicitly framed the whole approach around reading helpers.py/tests before coding, reasoning the hidden suite mirrors the public client's conventions rather than inventing shapes.

Systematically read every dev_tests file, mining the exact wire shapes it would touch: cell kind discriminator, spill/spill_range fields, {workbooks:[]} envelope, patch/pivot/validation bodies, and the full collab op/event protocol.
Probed environment for available libraries (all False), Python version, libreoffice, npm — grounding library choices in reality before committing to openpyxl + in-process engine.
Ran run.sh, and on the one failure resolved LET-bound LAMBDA dispatch correctly per Excel named-lambda semantics — though reactively rather than pre-emptively.
During hardening, wrote a targeted probe (SUM(OFFSET(...))) against the internal engine to verify reference-function semantics before finalizing.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent systematically mined every public test file and helpers.py for the shapes it touches (spill anchors/ghosts, error sentinels, collab/pivot/validation bodies, listing envelope), cross-checked against run.sh and conftest, and probed the environment — squarely matching the level-8 anchor. It falls short of 10 because orientation was largely front-loaded rather than continuous per-subsystem re-probing, and Excel edge-case grounding was more reactive (fixing after a test failure, one targeted probe) than the proactive surfacing and reasoning-through of ambiguous corners the top anchor requires.

dimensions.name: Subsystem decomposition & sequenced milestones

evidence.note: The sole explicit plan is a flat 4-step to-do (read contract, implement app+model+engine+IO+WebSockets, run tests, start server). The entire sprawling product is one undifferentiated 'implement' step — no subsystem decomposition, no dependency ordering among subsystems, no per-subsystem completion criteria.

The whole build lands in a single ~86KB monolithic patch, confirming the implementation was not sequenced into ordered milestones — engine, spill, functions, analyst surface, collab, XLSX, and SPA were all written in one pass rather than foundations-before-dependents.

Prose enumerates the major subsystems (CRUD, formulas, spill arrays, fill/sort/filter, CSV/XLSX, styling, validation, pivot, iterative calc, goal seek, WebSockets), showing subsystem awareness — but this is a coverage list, not a dependency-aware sequenced milestone plan with acceptance checks.

Coarse phase order is present: 'first pass broad, then use the public suite to tighten edge cases' (35), then targeted 'hardening pass' on hidden-suite-likely areas like OOXML/lookup (52,75). This gives a rough success signal (suite green) but not per-milestone done-checks or foundation-before-dependent sequencing.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent's planning is a flat, undifferentiated to-do that folds the entire product into a single implementation step executed as one monolithic patch — matching the anchor-3 description of feature-name lists without dependency ordering or per-item done-checks. It rises slightly above 3 because it maintains a sensible foundational phase order (understand contract first, verify after via run.sh, then a targeted hardening pass with a rough success signal) and shows explicit subsystem awareness in prose. But it falls clearly short of anchor 5, which requires decomposing the build into ordered subsystems (server/health, then cell+recompute core, then functions) with rough per-milestone signals — the agent never sequenced the implementation into subsystem milestones at all.

dimensions.name: Self-built verification beyond the smoke suite

evidence.note: Ran run.sh in deliberate slices (api/engine, then deps/spill/csv, then xlsx/pivot/locale/validation) to isolate contract/evaluator defects rather than one blind run — targeted use of the provided suite.
Ran the full visible suite (131 passed) after hardening changes — confirms green but this alone is only anchor-3 behavior.

Self-built restart-persistence check: created workbook+formula, restarted process, verified B1 recomputed to 42, inspected state.json/next_id. A deliberately constructed check targeting a hidden-suite risk beyond the smoke suite (matches one anchor-8/10 element).

Explicitly framed a 'hardening pass for hidden-suite behavior' and manually value-checked a function added beyond the public corpus (IFNA→'x'). Hidden-suite-motivated, but verification was a single spot value.

Final report cites only run.sh (131 passed) + restart persistence as verification — no perf-threshold timing, no independent openpyxl round-trip, no self-built value oracle or collab/spill checks beyond the provided suite.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent goes clearly beyond treating a green run.sh as done (anchor 3) and beyond mere ad-hoc sanity calls (anchor 5): it slices the suite to localize failures, and constructs a genuine restart-persistence verification plus hidden-suite-motivated spot checks for functions outside the public corpus. However, it does not design the breadth anchor 8 requires — no agent-authored performance timing against the stated thresholds, no independent openpyxl re-read round-trip, no self-built Excel value oracle beyond one function, and no independent spill/collab checks (all rely on the provided tests). This places it between anchors 5 and 8, at 6.

dimensions.name: Coverage tracking across the feature surface

evidence.note: Enumerated the full subsystem surface the tests cover (CRUD, formulas, spill, IO, validation, pivot, iterative calc, goal seek, collab) — an explicit up-front coverage inventory.
Created a 4-item plan with completed/in_progress/pending statuses, but never updated it again over the remaining ~45 steps despite finishing all items; the formal ledger was coarse and went stale.

Used the smoke suite as the coverage gauge: saw 130/131, isolated the one failing subsystem (LET-bound lambda), patched it, and reran the whole suite to confirm 131 pass and no regression — status tied to verification results.
Identified remaining-risk areas (OOXML round-trip, lookup/reference functions) and steered a targeted hardening pass, showing awareness of what was thin vs done, though only at prose granularity.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent kept a running, verification-tied picture of status — inventorying subsystems (25), gauging progress by test pass counts, catching the single failing case and re-verifying the full suite (45-52), and naming still-risky areas for hardening (75). But its formal ledger (the step-34 plan) was coarse and never updated, and there was no granular per-subsystem/per-function status tracking beyond aggregate test counts, so staleness and gaps crept in. This matches anchor 5, with only partial reach toward the tighter, continually-updated ledger of anchor 8.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on divergence

evidence.note: On the single failing smoke test (LET-bound LAMBDA yielding #NAME?), the agent diagnosed the true cause — dispatch resolving the binding as a named function instead of an env lambda — and fixed dispatch order rather than special-casing the test. Genuine root-cause correction (anchor 5).
Re-ran the full suite after the fix (131 passed) rather than just checking the one case, confirming the correction held — proper closure of the adjust-then-verify loop.

During hardening, recognized openpyxl's create_named_range couldn't produce the required defined-name form and switched to DefinedName; also reworked data-validation import ordering so imported rules wouldn't reject their own patches. Small but real layer-level design corrections when an API/flow contradicted the initial approach.
Caught missing python-multipart dependency during an import pass and added it before running — minor adaptive correction, but reactive to observed need.

Heavy up-front contract/library investigation meant most big assumptions were correct on first contact, so few foundational premises were falsified; hence little opportunity for (and no evidence of) anchor-8 re-architecture.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent never pressed on with broken assumptions (well above 0-3): every contradiction it encountered — the LAMBDA test failure, the openpyxl named-range API mismatch, the validation-import ordering, the missing multipart dep — was diagnosed at root cause and fixed by adjusting that feature's approach, matching anchor 5. It slightly exceeds 5 with a couple of localized layer reworks (DefinedName switch, DV import flow), but shows no evidence of detecting and re-architecting a foundational choice under blown perf or library-fidelity limits (anchor 8), largely because thorough up-front investigation left few premises falsified. Net observed level: 5.

dimensions.name: Scope allocation under breadth-exceeds-capacity

evidence.note: Deliberate breadth-first allocation: 'The first pass is intentionally broad, then I'll use the public suite to tighten edge cases' — secure wide coverage before depth.

Explicit hidden-suite-value reasoning: after visible suite green, invests a hardening pass specifically in OOXML round-trip and lookup/reference functions because those are 'easy places for graders to go beyond the public smoke tests.' Payoff-targeted allocation above mere prioritization.
Follows through on that triage — hardening OFFSET/reference metadata, more lookup modes, and XLSX preservation of validation/CF/defined names/styles, i.e. the identified high-risk corners.
Plan is coarse (4 generic steps) with no per-subsystem budget, stubbing, or deferral decisions; triage is qualitative, not an explicit resource-allocation ledger.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent goes beyond anchor 5's 'rough awareness' by explicitly allocating a hardening pass toward the specific subsystems it judges most likely for the hidden suite to probe (steps 52, 75), grounded in payoff reasoning, after deliberately securing broad coverage first (step 35). However it never consciously stubs or defers low-payoff exotica, never reasons about remaining budget, and never re-triages as evidence accrues — it simply built the whole surface and hardened the risky corners. That situates it between anchors 5 and 8, at a 6.

rubric.task_read: A very long-horizon, multi-component build: a full Excel-clone product (HTTP server, persistence, SPA, JSON+WebSocket API, a large formula engine with dynamic arrays/spilling/iterative calc/goal-seek, XLSX round-tripping, pivots, conditional formatting, locale input, collaboration). The wire contract is deliberately underspecified and must be reverse-engineered from an existing first-party client (/dev_tests/helpers.py); grading is on a hidden suite far larger than the provided smoke tests, against LibreOffice ground truth. Feature breadth vastly exceeds what can be built perfectly in any session, so a skilled practitioner would invest heavily in orientation, decomposition, self-built verification, and continuous triage — this is near the ceiling of meta-work demand.

dimensions.name: Contract reverse-engineering & Excel-semantics grounding
dimensions.description: Extracting the exact wire shapes from /dev_tests/helpers.py and grounding function/error behavior in real Excel-365 semantics before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The spec explicitly defers the wire shape to what helpers.py already calls, and grading uses a hidden suite plus LibreOffice ground truth. An agent that guesses shapes or invents semantics will fail broadly regardless of code quality; reading the client and probing the environment is the single highest-leverage act here.

anchors.0: Starts coding server/endpoints without reading helpers.py or run.sh; invents request/response shapes and function behavior from imagination.
anchors.3: Skims helpers.py once, grabs a couple of endpoint shapes, but leaves the cell `kind` discriminator, spill fields, and listing envelope guessed; no grounding in Excel edge-case semantics.
anchors.5: Reads helpers.py to derive the core cell/patch/listing shapes and runs the smoke suite to see current state; consults Excel behavior for the common functions being implemented.
anchors.8: Systematically mines helpers.py for every shape it touches (spill anchors/ghosts, error sentinels, fill/sort/filter/pivot/collab bodies), cross-checks against run.sh, and deliberately resolves ambiguous Excel semantics (criteria wildcards, spill materialization, LWW ordering, iterative fixed-point) by reasoning or targeted probes before committing.
anchors.10: Builds and maintains a precise internal model of the entire contract traced to concrete client call sites, proactively surfaces underspecified corners (locale canonicalization, XLSX openpyxl constraints, ghost-write rejection), and re-probes the client/environment whenever a new subsystem is entered rather than assuming — orientation is continuous and evidence-anchored throughout.

dimensions.name: Subsystem decomposition & sequenced milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking a sprawling product into an ordered hierarchy of subsystems (core CRUD+persistence+health, recompute engine, functions, dynamic arrays, analyst surface, collab, XLSX, SPA) each with an explicit done-check and a dependency-aware order.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The surface spans dozens of loosely coupled features with hard dependencies (e.g. recompute engine underpins everything; spilling underpins dynamic arrays; XLSX/pivot depend on the cell model). Without deliberate sequencing an agent thrashes across half-built subsystems and lands nothing verifiable.

anchors.0: No structure; jumps between random features (a distribution function here, a WebSocket handler there) with no ordering or completion criteria.
anchors.3: A flat undifferentiated to-do of feature names with no dependency ordering and no notion of when each is 'done'.
anchors.5: Identifies major subsystems and tackles a sensible foundational order (server/health/persistence, then a working cell+recompute core, then functions), with rough per-milestone success signals.
anchors.8: A dependency-aware milestone plan where each milestone has a concrete acceptance check (endpoint returns X, run.sh subset green, spill materializes), foundations sequenced before dependents, and the plan reflects that the engine/spill core gates most later work.
anchors.10: A crisp, layered milestone hierarchy that sequences the whole build for maximum verified coverage, explicitly ordering by both dependency and grading payoff, with each milestone independently demonstrable — and the structure is revisited and re-ordered as understanding of the contract deepens.

dimensions.name: Self-built verification beyond the smoke suite
dimensions.description: Deliberately constructing checks — running run.sh, adding targeted tests, cross-checking against Excel/LibreOffice values, verifying XLSX via openpyxl, exercising performance bounds — rather than trusting the non-exhaustive provided tests.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The spec warns the dev_tests are a small smoke suite and grading is a much larger hidden suite against held-out ground truth. Passing run.sh proves almost nothing; only agent-designed verification (value correctness, round-trips, error mapping, perf thresholds) predicts hidden-suite success.

anchors.0: Never runs the tests or the server against real requests; assumes code works because it was written.
anchors.3: Runs run.sh and treats green as done; no checks for the many behaviors the smoke suite doesn't cover.
anchors.5: Runs run.sh plus some ad-hoc manual API calls to sanity-check the features built, catching obvious breakage.
anchors.8: Designs verification targeted at hidden-suite risk: checks formula values against known Excel results, verifies error-sentinel/HTTP-status mapping, round-trips CSV/XLSX (re-reading with openpyxl), exercises spill/ghost rejection and collab ordering, and checks at least one performance scenario against its threshold.
anchors.10: Establishes a reusable verification harness spanning subsystems (value oracles, round-trip diffs, perf timing, restart-persistence checks) run repeatedly as the build grows, treats any divergence from Excel/LibreOffice semantics as a failing signal to chase, and calibrates confidence per subsystem from evidence rather than assumption.

dimensions.name: Coverage tracking across the feature surface
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of which of the many subsystems/functions are done, working, or broken, and detecting when effort is stuck or circling on one area at the expense of the whole.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With this many features and a long horizon, it is easy to lose the plot — over-polishing one function family while whole subsystems remain unbuilt, or re-debugging the same recompute bug in circles. Accurate done-vs-remaining tracking is what sustains forward progress.

anchors.0: No sense of overall state; cannot say what's built vs pending; repeats the same fix attempts without noticing.
anchors.3: Vague recollection of progress; discovers late that major subsystems were never started or silently regressed.
anchors.5: Keeps a running list of completed vs remaining subsystems and generally knows current status, though staleness or gaps creep in.
anchors.8: Maintains an accurate, updated ledger of subsystem status tied to verification results, notices when a subsystem is consuming disproportionate time, and catches regressions in previously-working areas.
anchors.10: Sustains a precise, evidence-backed picture of the whole surface across the entire horizon, proactively detects stuck/circular states early and names them, and uses the status picture to reallocate attention deliberately rather than drifting.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on divergence
dimensions.description: Revising design, approach, or plan when reality contradicts assumptions — wrong wire shape, mismatched Excel semantics, performance blown, a library that can't round-trip — instead of pressing on with a falsified premise.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Many assumptions here are likely wrong on first contact (guessed shapes, naive full-recompute that violates perf bounds, an XLSX library that drops conditional formatting). The ability to detect the falsification and re-architect rather than patch around it determines whether the system converges.

anchors.0: Ignores contradicting evidence (failing tests, timeouts, shape mismatches) and keeps building on the broken assumption.
anchors.3: Reacts to failures with local hacks that paper over symptoms without revisiting the wrong underlying design.
anchors.5: When a test or check fails, diagnoses and fixes the real cause, adjusting the approach for that feature.
anchors.8: Recognizes when a foundational choice is wrong (e.g. recompute strategy can't meet perf, a library can't satisfy XLSX fidelity, an assumed shape is contradicted by helpers.py) and re-architects the affected layer deliberately, updating the plan accordingly.
anchors.10: Treats divergence as information: quickly isolates falsified assumptions, weighs re-design vs workaround explicitly, pivots decisively while protecting already-working subsystems, and folds the lesson back into the plan and verification so the same class of error is caught earlier.

dimensions.name: Scope allocation under breadth-exceeds-capacity
dimensions.description: Deliberately allocating finite effort across a feature surface too large to finish perfectly — choosing which functions/subsystems to fully implement, which to stub, and which to defer to maximize graded coverage.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The catalog (hundreds of functions plus collab, XLSX, pivots, locale, goal-seek) almost certainly exceeds what can be built flawlessly. A skilled agent explicitly triages for marginal payoff on the hidden suite rather than either perfecting one corner or spreading so thin that nothing is solid — a resource-allocation judgment distinct from mere ordering.

anchors.0: No triage: builds whatever comes to mind, commonly over-investing in a narrow area while leaving breadth untouched, or leaving core paths half-working.
anchors.3: Implicitly picks features by convenience with no reasoning about coverage or payoff.
anchors.5: Prioritizes clearly high-value, high-frequency features (core CRUD, common functions, spilling) before exotic ones, with rough awareness that not everything will be finished.
anchors.8: Makes explicit allocation decisions — securing broad correct coverage of common behavior first, consciously stubbing or deferring low-payoff exotica, and defending the choices in terms of hidden-suite value and remaining budget.
anchors.10: Continuously re-triages as budget burns and evidence accrues, trading depth for breadth (or vice versa) with explicit expected-value reasoning, ensuring the delivered system is broadly correct and coherent rather than a few polished islands amid unbuilt or broken subsystems.
